description: T3-1 multi-provider: run Claude, Codex, and Grok behind the existing AgentDriver seam (src/agent/driver.ts), with the UI adapting honestly to each provider's real capabilities instead of assuming Claude's. Adds an AgentCapabilities descriptor, a provider registry + install probe, CodexDriver (one process per turn, `codex exec --json`, no interactive approval) and GrokDriver (Claude-like: `-p --output-format streaming-json`, token deltas, real reasoning text, total_cost_usd), a per-thread provider column, a composer provider chip locked after turn 1, and capability-driven permission/transcript/avatar rendering. Manual failover only; no cross-provider context transfer. Source PRD: prd-conan-multi-provider.md. NOTE for the executing agent: read AGENTS.md + HANDOFF.md first - Conan is chat-primary; run the gateway with `npm start` (not npm run dev); verify BOTH :3747 and :5173 after any gateway restart; browser-verify on a throwaway CONAN_PORT/CONAN_UI_PORT stack with CONAN_ALLOWED_ORIGINS set, never on :3747. Subscription auth only - never introduce ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

userStories.title: Probe + pin provider capabilities as test fixtures
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the real headless behavior of codex and grok captured as fixtures, so every driver is built against verified truth rather than --help guesses.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `src/agent/fixtures/` with the observed NDJSON event streams for codex (`codex exec --json`) and grok (`grok -p --output-format streaming-json`), captured from a real run in a temp dir

Document the verified capability matrix: codex = no token deltas, no interactive approval, one process per turn, token counts only (no USD); grok = token deltas, readable reasoning text, total_cost_usd, --resume

Explicitly probe and record two open questions: (a) does grok support interactive tool approval headlessly in `--permission-mode default`, (b) can grok switch permission mode mid-session. Record the ANSWER, and if a capability is unavailable say so plainly
Note the codex stdin footgun: `codex exec` reads stdin when piped ('Reading additional input from stdin...') - the driver must pass the prompt as an argument and give the child stdin: 'ignore'
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Facts-first story - everything downstream depends on it. Probes cost a few cents of real agent usage; keep prompts trivial (e.g. 'Reply with exactly: probe-ok') and run in a temp dir, never the conan repo. Suggested skills: none.

userStories.title: Add AgentCapabilities to the driver seam
userStories.description: As a developer, I want each driver to declare what it can actually do, so the UI can adapt without ever branching on a provider name.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `AgentCapabilities` to src/agent/driver.ts: streamingDeltas, interactiveApproval, livePermissionSwitch, costUsd, reasoningText, resume, and permissionModes (array of {id, label, description} in the provider's own vocabulary)
Add `readonly capabilities: AgentCapabilities` to the AgentDriver interface

ClaudeDriver declares its verified descriptor: streamingDeltas true, interactiveApproval true, livePermissionSwitch true, costUsd true, reasoningText FALSE (D2 - headless claude redacts thinking text), resume true, permissionModes = default/plan/acceptEdits/bypassPermissions with their existing labels
No behavior change: the chat works exactly as before for Claude
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Pure seam widening, no runtime change. Depends on US-001's verified matrix. Suggested skills: codebase-design.

userStories.title: Provider registry + install probe route
userStories.description: As a user, I want Conan to know which agent CLIs are installed, so the composer can offer the ones I can actually use.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `src/agent/registry.ts`: one entry per provider with id ('claude'|'codex'|'grok'), display name, avatar letter (C/X/G), binary name, capabilities, and a driver factory
Detect installed binaries via a login-shell PATH probe, mirroring src/doctor/claude.ts (packaged app PATH gotcha - use an interactive login shell); cache with a TTL
GET /api/agent/providers returns [{id, name, avatarLetter, installed, version|null, capabilities}]; token-gated + covered by the CORS reflector like every other gateway route
An uninstalled provider is reported installed:false with no error - never a hang or a raw stack
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: The registry is a data table, not a plugin framework - keep it small. Suggested skills: none.

userStories.title: CodexDriver - spawn, parse, resume, interrupt
userStories.description: As a user, I want to run a chat on Codex, so I can keep working when Claude credits run out.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `src/agent/codex.ts` implementing AgentDriver against `codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check -C <cwd>` with the prompt as an argument and stdin ignored

Parse the JSONL into normalized AgentEvents: thread.started to system (thread_id is the resume key), item.completed(agent_message) to assistant-text, command/file items to tool-use/tool-result, turn.completed to result (token usage; costUsd null)
Multi-turn continuity: the first turn spawns fresh, later turns spawn `codex exec resume <thread_id>` - verify a 2-turn conversation actually retains context
Map permission to `--sandbox read-only|workspace-write|danger-full-access`; capabilities declare interactiveApproval false, streamingDeltas false, costUsd false, livePermissionSwitch false
respondPermission() is an explicit no-op (documented, not silently swallowed); interrupt() kills the in-flight turn process and surfaces an honest exit event
Unknown event types are ignored rather than thrown, so a CLI version bump can't crash the parser
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: The structurally-alien provider - this story is what proves the seam. Parser tests should run against the US-001 fixtures (no live calls in tests). Suggested skills: none.

userStories.title: GrokDriver - spawn, parse, resume, interrupt

Capabilities declare streamingDeltas true, reasoningText TRUE, costUsd true, resume true; interactiveApproval and livePermissionSwitch set to whatever US-001 actually verified
Map permission modes onto grok's `--permission-mode` (default/acceptEdits/plan/bypassPermissions)
Multi-turn continuity verified: a 2-turn conversation retains context via --resume
Unknown event types are ignored rather than thrown

Tests pass

userStories.title: WS launch frame carries provider; build driver from the registry
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the /ws/agent handler to instantiate whichever provider the chat asked for, so the seam is actually used.
acceptanceCriteria: The prompt/launch frame accepts a `provider` field; src/agent/index.ts builds the driver from the registry instead of hard-instantiating ClaudeDriver

userStories.title: Composer provider chip (locked after the first turn)

Uninstalled providers appear disabled with an explanatory tooltip (e.g. 'codex not found on PATH') rather than being hidden
The chosen provider rides the prompt frame and LOCKS after the first turn, exactly like the model/cwd chips (reuse the existing `locked` treatment)

userStories.title: Capability-driven permission chip
userStories.description: As a user, I want the permission control to show what my chosen agent can actually enforce, not a Claude control it will ignore.
acceptanceCriteria: The permission chip renders its options from capabilities.permissionModes - never a hard-coded Claude list and never a branch on provider id
On Claude it still reads Supervised / Plan / Accept edits / Full access; on Codex it reads its real sandbox options (read-only / workspace-write / full-access) and Supervised is ABSENT, not inert
When capabilities.livePermissionSwitch is false, the chip explains the change applies to the next turn instead of silently pretending to switch live
When capabilities.interactiveApproval is false, no approval UI is offered for that thread
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build passes
Verify in browser using automate-browser skill: compare the chip on a Claude thread vs a Codex thread
userStories.notes: The honesty story - the whole point of the capability model. Suggested skills: automate-browser.

userStories.title: Capability-driven transcript (deltas, reasoning, cost)
userStories.description: As a user, I want the transcript to reflect what my agent actually reports, so nothing looks broken or fabricated.
acceptanceCriteria: When capabilities.streamingDeltas is false (Codex), the transcript shows a working indicator while the turn runs instead of an idle streaming caret, then renders the completed message
When capabilities.costUsd is false (Codex), the per-turn footer shows token counts instead of a fabricated or blank dollar figure
When capabilities.reasoningText is true (Grok), the previously-dormant collapsed reasoning UI renders the streamed thought text; it stays hidden for Claude, where the text is redacted (D2)
No provider-name branching in the components - all three behaviors read from capabilities
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build passes
Verify in browser using automate-browser skill: a Codex turn (no caret, token footer) and a Grok turn (reasoning expands)
userStories.notes: Un-shelves the D2 reasoning UI for Grok - a real user-visible win from this PRD. Suggested skills: automate-browser.
